{{Short description|Generalization of conditional expectation}}
{{more citations needed|date=November 2014}}

In [[mathematics]], '''non-commutative conditional expectation''' is a generalization of the notion of [[conditional expectation]] in classical [[probability]]. The space of essentially bounded measurable functions on a <math>\sigma</math>-finite measure space <math>(X, \mu)</math> is the canonical example of a [[Abelian von Neumann algebra|commutative von Neumann algebra]]. For this reason, the theory of von Neumann algebras is sometimes referred to as noncommutative [[Measure (mathematics)|measure theory]]. The intimate connections of [[probability theory]] with measure theory suggest that one may be able to extend the classical ideas in probability to a noncommutative setting by studying those ideas on general von Neumann algebras.

For von Neumann algebras with a faithful normal tracial state, for example finite von Neumann algebras, the notion of conditional expectation is especially useful.

==Formal definition==
Let <math>\mathcal{R} \subseteq \mathcal{S} </math> be von Neumann algebras (<math>\mathcal{S}</math> and <math>\mathcal{R}</math> may be general [[C*-algebras]] as well), a positive, linear mapping <math>\Phi</math> of <math>\mathcal{S}</math> onto <math>\mathcal{R}</math>  is said to be a ''conditional expectation'' (of <math>\mathcal{S}</math> onto <math>\mathcal{R}</math>) when <math>\Phi(I)=I</math> and <math>\Phi(R_1SR_2) = R_1\Phi(S)R_2</math> if <math>R_1, R_2 \in \mathcal{R}</math> and <math>S \in \mathcal{S}</math>.

==Applications==
===Sakai's theorem===
Let <math>\mathcal{B}</math> be a C*-subalgebra of the C*-algebra <math>\mathfrak{A}, \varphi_0</math> an idempotent linear mapping of <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> onto <math>\mathcal{B}</math> such that <math>\|\varphi_0\| = 1, \mathfrak{A}</math> acting on <math>\mathcal{H}</math> the universal representation of <math>\mathfrak{A}</math>. Then <math>\varphi_0</math> extends uniquely to an ultraweakly continuous idempotent linear mapping <math>\varphi</math> of <math>\mathfrak{A}^{-}</math>, the weak-operator closure of <math>\mathfrak{A}</math>, onto <math>\mathcal{B}^{-}</math>, the weak-operator closure of <math>\mathcal{B}</math>.

In the above setting, a result<ref>Tomiyama J., ''On the projection of norm one in W*-algebras'', Proc. Japan Acad. (33) (1957), Theorem 1, Pg. 608</ref> first proved by Tomiyama may be formulated in the following manner.

'''Theorem.''' Let <math>\mathfrak{A}, \mathcal{B}, \varphi, \varphi_0</math> be as described above. Then <math>\varphi</math> is a conditional expectation from <math>\mathfrak{A}^{-}</math> onto <math>\mathcal{B}^{-}</math> and <math>\varphi_0</math> is a conditional expectation from <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> onto <math>\mathcal{B}</math>.

With the aid of Tomiyama's theorem an elegant proof of [[Von Neumann algebra#The predual|Sakai's result]] on the characterization of those C*-algebras that are *-isomorphic to von Neumann algebras may be given.
